fixes.explanation: Surplus is it. Jesus says, "…they all contributed out of their surplus…" That means what they had left over. Then He sets her beside them: she out of her poverty put in all she had to live on. Think of a cookie jar: they gave from the extras, and she gave from the bottom of it.

That's an easy mix-up, because that person is in the middle of the sentence. But look at who says "I." The Lord says, "Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet." So the Lord does the making, and the one at His right hand is the one told to sit.

Long robes, yes. Jesus says the scribes "…like to walk around in long robes…" Notice He says they like walking around in them. I think they were doing a lot of strolling. If I had a robe that long, my apron would be jealous.
Sackcloth isn't what Jesus names. He says the scribes "…like to walk around in long robes…" That's the clothing He points to. Sackcloth never comes up in this passage.

Jesus doesn't say that, friend. He says the scribes "…defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers." The prayers are described as being for a show, right alongside the defrauding of widows. I think that stings, and I'd rather say so than skip past it.

Yes, and this is the part that gets me. Jesus says, "Truly I tell you," and then, "this poor widow has put in more than all the others." Her gift was two small copper coins. And He says she put in more than the rest.

I know it sounds backwards, but it's true. Jesus says, "Truly I tell you," and then, "this poor widow has put in more than all the others." Her gift was two small copper coins. Jesus still says she put in more than all the others.
